pattern: WAI-ARIA APG Date Picker Dialog, non-modal variant, for a range: a labelled role=group containing two labelled segmented date fields (Date Input), a button with aria-haspopup=dialog inside the end field, and a role=dialog popup containing a range-selecting Calendar grid (one or two months).

roles.role: group (Date Input), each with its own visually hidden label

aria.value: Help text id when description is set
Id of the field's visually hidden label (startLabel / endLabel, default "Start date" / "End date")
"Choose dates", or "Change dates, <long start date> to <long end date>" when a range is set

aria.element: segments of the field that shows the error
aria.value: Set by that Date Input when its message is shown

keyboard.action: Open (or close) the calendar; focus moves to the range start, else the typed start date, else today.

keyboard.context: Date segment of either field focused
keyboard.action: Open the calendar (the segment value does not change).
Arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Shift+PageUp/PageDown as in Calendar, across all visible months.

keyboard.context: Day focused, no pending first day
keyboard.action: Pick the first day of the range; it is announced and the popup stays open.
Pick the last day (either order), write both fields, close the popup (closeOnSelect), and focus the calendar button.
Close the popup, discarding a pending first day, and return focus to the calendar button. Inside a Dialog, only the popup closes.
Moves through month buttons and the day; leaving the popup (other than to the calendar button) closes it.
As in Date Input; Tab moves from the start field to the end field.

focus: Opening moves focus into the grid; closing with focus inside the popup returns it to the calendar button. Outside pointer presses close the popup. The button and popup sit inside the end field, so moving focus between the end segments, the button, and the popup does not mark the end field touched; leaving the start field marks the start field touched.
notes: The segments remain the primary input; the calendar is an alternative (APG).
The popup is non-modal: focus is not trapped, and the rest of the page stays reachable.
Each field has its own accessible name (visually hidden) inside the labelled group, so screen readers announce the group label and 'Start date' or 'End date'.
Range errors are shown on the field they concern (for example a reversed range on the end field) through that Date Input's message and aria-describedby.
The calendar names the first and last day ('start of range', 'end of range') and announces the pending first day through a polite live region.
A typed start or end day rejected by isDateDisabled produces a localized message, so the typed and picked paths agree.
knownCaveats: Screen-reader behavior (group and field names, dialog announcement, range day names, the pending-day announcement) has not yet been manually verified with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver.
